thread:
maria: quick bring-up notes for Lite9B-int6 (sideload) on GTN chat slices. short TL;DR then numbers.

jon: pls paste the numbers.

maria: TL;DR: strong parity on chat-short, ~1.8pt drop on long/instruction slices, ~20% lower token cost, p99 tail needs attention. full scorecard below.

maria: ```
model: Lite9B-int6 (sideload)
slices: chat-short | chat-long | instruction-clarity
chat-short QA: 92.0%  (prod baseline 92.3)
chat-long QA: 84.4%   (prod baseline 86.2)
instruction QA: 87.2% (prod baseline 88.9)
latency: p50=45ms p95=185ms p99=410ms
throughput: ~45 req/s on 2xA10g (continuous batching)
token-cost est: $0.0018 / 1k tokens (baseline: $0.0023)
regression note: longform recall -1.8 absolute vs Nova7B-int8
```

keith: p99 looks like kvcache churn + small-batch interference. if we pin warm-KV workers tail halves. infra cost ~+8%.

nora: product question: net savings after infra bump?

maria: rough mix calc (60% short,30% long,10% instr): token savings ~18%. with warm-KV infra +8%, net platform cost down ~10-11%.

jon: can prompt tricks recover the long drop?

maria: 2-shot anchors recovered ~0.6-0.9pts. best recovery came from int6-safe quant profile: +1.2pts but p50 increases ~8% and throughput drops slightly (effective cost +6%).

nora: options?

maria: 1) staged roll: Lite9B-int6 for short only, keep Nova for long. 2) int6-safe + warm-KV global -> near parity, ~6-7% net savings. 3) hold until kernel fixes.

jon: i'd pilot option 2 on 10% traffic with canary thresholds. suggest rollback if any slice drops >1.0 pt or p99 latency worsens >30% for 24h.

keith: i'll estimate infra delta and prototype warm-KV config, posting numbers later today.
